headline: P0066 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share well above expected, but documentation review mostly supports the 99215 claims; pattern leans toward a legitimately complex panel, with caveats
rationale: P0066 billed 99215 on 15.0% of 452 claims against an expected 3.9% given patient complexity (risk-adjusted score 4.49, z vs peers 1.46). The provider's 99215 share runs about 2-6x the all-provider rate in every complexity stratum, including 0-condition patients (12.9% vs 2.1%, 8 of 62 visits). The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include acute-only diagnoses such as J06.9 (C0029774, C0030029), N39.0 (C0029903, C0029960) and M54.50 (C0030040, C0030076). However, the documentation review, which is the stronger evidence, does not show upcoding. Of 19 documented 99215 claims, 3 (15.8%) were unsupported, below the all-provider rate of 24.2%. The 99213 and 99214 unsupported rates (7.1%, 8.4%) match peers. Several documented 99215s show high MDM and 41-51 minutes (C0029676, C0029736, C0029912, C0029968). The 3 unsupported 99215 examples (C0029709, C0029756, C0029806) were all on low-complexity patients and documented at moderate MDM. That is a pattern worth a targeted check, but 3 is a small number. The overall pattern is consistent with a more complex panel than the claims-based complexity measure captures, not with systematic upcoding. Only 25.7% of claims have records, and 19 documented 99215s is a modest sample.
next_steps: Pull records for more 99215 claims on patients with 0-1 chronic conditions (e.g., C0029774, C0030029, C0029903, C0030040) to test whether low-complexity 99215s are disproportionately unsupported.
Review the 3 unsupported 99215 claims (C0029709, C0029756, C0029806) for a common pattern such as reliance on time vs MDM or a shared template.

Check whether the claims-based chronic-condition count understates acuity (e.g., missing diagnoses, acute complexity, care coordination) to explain the elevated 99215 share in the 0-1 condition strata.
If expanded sampling stays at or below the all-provider unsupported rate, consider closing with education rather than escalation.
